summary: On December 19, 2023, Hipgnosis Songs Fund's board delayed its interim results (six months to end of September 2023), saying Citrin Cooperman's latest valuation was materially higher than recent sector transactions imply. MBW argues this is a veiled statement aimed at Hipgnosis Song Management's call option and Citrin Cooperman's 8.5% discount rate. JP Morgan analyst Christopher Brown called it an early blow to the board's credibility and suggested applying an additional discount rate.
one_line: Hipgnosis Songs Fund's board delayed its interim results, objecting to Citrin Cooperman's valuation, prompting JP Morgan criticism and questions about HSM's call option and the discount rate.
key_facts: On December 19, 2023, the Hipgnosis Songs Fund board, led by Chairman Rob Naylor, announced its results for the six months to end of September 2023 would be published sometime before the close of December 31.
The HSF board said Citrin Cooperman's valuation was "materially higher than the valuation implied by proposed and recent transactions in the sector".
Hipgnosis Songs Capital's proposed purchase of assets for $440 million (pre-costs), or $417.5 million (post-costs), was rejected by HSF shareholders earlier in 2023.

On December 11, HSF announced the sale of 20,000 "non-core" songs to an unnamed buyer (possibly Kobalt Music Group) for $23.1 million, a 14.2% discount to Citrin Cooperman's September 30 valuation of that portfolio.
HSF's board sought an opinion from Hipgnosis Song Management, majority owned by Blackstone-managed and/or advised funds, which gave a "heavily caveated" opinion.
Hipgnosis Song Management responded that it had fulfilled its duties on the independent valuation and interim results in a timely and efficient manner.
HSF's own reports say Citrin Cooperman was appointed by the Board, which is "ultimately and solely responsible" for overseeing the valuation.
Citrin Cooperman keeps an 8.5% discount rate despite interest rate rises over the past 12-18 months; raising it would instantly lower HSF's portfolio valuation.
JP Morgan analyst Christopher Brown said a 0.5% rise in the discount rate (8.5% to 9.0%) would cut the portfolio's fair value by 7.9%, about a 10% reduction in NAV on a leveraged basis.
Brown said he was surprised no second valuer was used, since Kroll was appointed to consider the reasonableness of Citrin Cooperman's assumptions for the results to end of March 2023.
Brown said he would not be surprised to see Citrin Cooperman resign, and JP Morgan kept its 'overweight' rating on HSF.
HSF appointed activist investor Christopher Mills as a non-exec Director the previous week.
HSF benefits in Q4 from cuts on Taylor Swift's 1989 (Taylor's Version), Lover, Michael Buble's Christmas album and Mariah Carey's All I Want For Christmas Is You.
